opex.note: Money set aside for customer loans that may not be repaid.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Legal, finance and head office — up 39%, partly on payroll taxes from the CEO's vesting stock awards.

footerNote: Robinhood does not report a separate cost of revenue; 'Brokerage and transaction' — the direct cost of executing customers' trades — is shown as the direct cost here. Net income of $556M is attributable to Robinhood; there was no non-controlling interest this quarter.
oneTimers: General and administrative costs rose 39% to $185M, partly on payroll taxes triggered when the CEO's 2019 market-based stock awards vested as the share price climbed — a cost that grows with the stock price, not with the business.
otherDetail: Other income (loss), net was −$1M — small next to the main business.

segments.name: Transaction-based revenues
segments.note: What customers pay to trade — crypto brought in $268M, options $304M, equities $86M.

segments.name: Net interest revenues
segments.note: Interest on customers' cash and margin loans, plus securities lending.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Robinhood Gold subscriptions and other smaller income.

takeaways.text: Total Platform Assets rose 119% to $333B, with a record $20.4B of net deposits in the quarter and $68.3B over the past twelve months.
takeaways.title: Customers keep piling in assets

takeaways.text: Robinhood Gold subscribers rose 77% to a record 3.9M, helping Other revenues double to $88M; average revenue per user rose 82% to $191.
takeaways.title: Gold becomes a real business

takeaways.text: Crypto revenue rose more than 300% to $268M — over a third of all transaction revenue — alongside options at $304M, up 50%, and equities at $86M, up 132%.
takeaways.title: Crypto is the swing factor

verdict: Robinhood's revenue doubled to a record $1.27B as crypto and options trading boomed — and profit more than tripled to $556M, with 11 business lines now each bringing in roughly $100M or more a year.
